newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares succumb to selling pressures.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares succumb to selling pressures.

text.p: Singapore shares succumbed to more selling pressures on Tuesday morning as institutions stayed sidelined and retail buyers cautious, dealers said.
Blue chips stocks were broadly lower although some selective buying was seen in electronics and foreign bank stocks.
Dealers said usual interest in Malaysian over-the-counter stocks was subdued in favour of newly-listed initial public offerings and a sprinkling of local small capitalisation issues.
At the lunch break, the Straits Times Industrials Index was 4.90 points lower at 1,986.18 on a thin volume of 42 million lots. Gainers just outnumbered losers at 121 to 117.
Dealers said curbs on property prices and higher water and electricity costs were seen crimping company profits.
"With speculative hype out of property and running costs going up, companies will have to survive on pure earning power," a local brokerage dealer said.
Among actives was debutante Australand, which hit a new high at Australian $1.53 and was up five cents at S$1.50 midday.
SIA foreign climbed to a high of S$12.40, aided by reports it would buy a third of Australia's Ansett airlines, but dropped back to end the session unchanged at S$12.20.
